evidence: app/package.json:7-13 — pinned to next 16.4.3 / react 19.3.1, both current stable (16.4.3 released 2026-10-23)
app/next.config.mjs:1-4 — empty config object: no experimental or preview flags at all
app/app/pokemon/[name]/page.tsx:27-28 — Promise params/searchParams, the required (not experimental) API in Next 16
reach.rationale: Zero experimental, preview, RC or canary APIs; even the recently-stable Next 16 features (Cache Components, proxy.ts, updateTag, React Compiler, next/image changes) are all avoided in favor of APIs that have been stable since the 13/14/15 era.

evidence: app/next.config.mjs:1-4 — nothing to contain; config carries no flags
app/lib/api.ts:20-38 — all data access funnels through one apiFetch/cached module, so nothing framework-novel leaks into routes
app/app/layout.tsx:4-6 and app/app/page.tsx:4-5 — the only 'modernization risk' is the repeated force-dynamic/no-store block, a 3-line idiom duplicated per route
containment.rationale: There are no experimental APIs to contain; the single non-trivial choice (no-store fetch behavior required by SPEC.md) is centralized in lib/api.ts and one repeated config block.

evidence: app/lib/api.ts:24-28 — fetch with cache:'no-store' satisfies the spec's 'live data at request time' requirement without reaching for Cache Components
app/app/layout.tsx:4-6 — force-dynamic/no-store used because SPEC.md forbids build-time prerendering, a legitimate need
app/components/HomeBrowser.tsx:82-86 — window.history.replaceState keeps URL state in sync using plain DOM history instead of any newer router primitive
justification.rationale: No experimental APIs are used, and the conservative choices are each justified by the spec's live-data and SSR requirements; nothing reads as novelty for its own sake.

findings.issue: fetchCache = 'force-no-store' is redundant on top of dynamic = 'force-dynamic', and the whole dynamic/revalidate/fetchCache block is duplicated across every route (app/app/page.tsx:4-5, app/app/types/page.tsx:4-5, app/app/[...slug]/page.tsx:4-5, app/app/pokemon/[name]/page.tsx:24, app/app/types/[name]/page.tsx:9)
findings.suggestion: Set the behavior once in the root layout (or in lib/api.ts, which already passes cache:'no-store' per request) and drop the per-route repetition; note these segment configs are superseded if the team later opts into Next 16's cacheComponents, so keeping them in one place lowers future migration cost

findings.issue: params/searchParams are typed by hand as Promise<Record<...>> instead of the PageProps typegen helpers Next 15.5+/16 provides
findings.suggestion: Optional modernization only: use PageProps<'/'> and PageProps<'/pokemon/[name]'> via npx next typegen for route-checked typing; the current form is still fully stable

summary: This is a deliberately conservative Next.js 16 app: the only framework surfaces touched are the long-stable App Router basics — Link, useRouter, Metadata/generateMetadata, Promise params/searchParams, and the classic dynamic/no-store segment configs — with an empty next.config and no unstable_/experimental_ identifiers anywhere. None of Next 16's newer features (Cache Components, proxy.ts, updateTag, React Compiler, next/image patterns) are used; the one place modernization would bite is the duplicated force-dynamic/fetchCache block that a future cacheComponents migration would rewrite. Experimentalness is effectively zero, which for a spec that mandates live request-time data is the right call.
